steps.title: Verification of Work Eligibility
steps.description: Strict verification of EU/EEA citizenship or valid single permit status for work in Belgium.

steps.title: Contract Drafting
steps.description: Drafting a locally compliant employment contract in the correct regional language (Dutch for Flanders, French for Wallonia, either/both for Brussels).

steps.title: Dimona Declaration
steps.description: Immediate declaration of the start of employment to the Belgian Social Security (ONSS) - mandatory before the employee starts.

steps.title: Work Rules Acknowledgement
steps.description: Ensuring the employee receives and signs a copy of the company's internal 'Arbeidsreglement' (Work Rules).

steps.title: Medical Examination
steps.description: Arranging a mandatory health check with an external occupational health service for specific job roles.

steps.title: Benefits Enrollment
steps.description: Setting up mandatory and optional benefits like meal vouchers, eco-vouchers, and group insurance.

items.text: Automatic Wage Indexation: Salaries are tied to the 'Health Index'. When inflation hits a certain threshold, all salaries in the relevant Parity Committee must increase.
The 13.85% Holiday Pay for Manual Workers: Manual workers receive their holiday pay via a national fund (RJV/ONVA), while white-collar workers receive it directly from the employer.
Parity Committees (PC): Belgium has over 100 industrial sectors (e.g., PC 200 for white-collar). Each has its own rules for overtime, bonuses, and minimum wages.
Language sensitivity is paramount. Using the wrong language in a contract (e.g., French for a Flanders-based seat) can lead to the contract being declared null and void.
Termination for 'Urgent Reason': Extremely difficult to prove and requires immediate action within 3 business days of the incident.
Eco-vouchers: An additional tax-free benefit (up to €250/year) intended for environmentally friendly purchases, common in many parity committees.

faqs.question: Can I hire interns through an EOR in Belgium?
faqs.answer: Yes, but Belgium has specific 'Professional Immersion Internships' (BIS/IFP) regulations that define minimum compensation and duration.

faqs.question: What is the probation period in Belgium?
faqs.answer: Since 2014, formal probation periods have been abolished for standard contracts, replaced by shorter notice periods in the first few months.

faqs.question: Does the EOR handle the 'Double Holiday Pay'?
faqs.answer: Yes, EOR providers calculate and manage the statutory 92% supplement paid to white-collar workers annually.

faqs.question: What is the 30% rule for expats?
faqs.answer: Belgium has a new expat regime allowing for 30% of the gross salary to be considered tax-free 'costs proper to the employer', subject to conditions.

steps.title: Data Collection & Timesheets
steps.description: Collecting hours worked, overtime (subject to CLA rules), sick leave certificados, and expense claims for the current month.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Calculating withholding taxes (Précompte professionnel) and social security contributions based on the employee's family situation and parity committee.

steps.title: Meal & Eco-vouchers Ordering
steps.description: Calculating the number of vouchers based on days worked and placing the order with providers (Sodexo/Edenred/Monizze).

steps.title: Declaration to RSZ/ONSS
steps.description: Submitting the DMFA (quarterly social security declaration) and monthly withholding tax returns via the government portal.

steps.title: Payment Execution
steps.description: Executing SEPA payments to employees, tax authorities, and social security funds by the legal deadlines.

steps.title: Payslip Generation
steps.description: Issuing digital payslips (Fiche de paie / Loonbrief) and updating the individual year-to-date accounts.

items.text: Collective Labor Agreements (CLAs): Most payroll rules in Belgium come from sector-specific agreements rather than just federal law.
Mobility Budget: Many companies now offer a mobility budget where employees can swap their company car for housing costs or other transport modes tax-free.
Commuting allowances for cyclists are particularly generous and tax-exempt up to specific per-km rates.
Double Holiday Pay (92%): This is a major cash flow consideration for employers every May/June.
Student Work: Reduced social security rates apply for student work up to 600 hours per year.
Working Time Reduction (ADV/RTT): Many 40-hour contracts grant 12 additional rest days per year to reach the legal 38-hour average.

items.title: Indexation
items.text: Wages are automatically indexed to inflation.

items.title: Holiday Pay
items.text: Double holiday pay is mandatory in May/June.

items.title: 13th Month
items.text: Most sectors require an end-of-year 13th month bonus.

steps.title: Gross Salary Base
steps.description: Starting with the contractually agreed monthly gross salary (usually for 13.92 months).

steps.title: RSZ Deduction
steps.description: Subtracting 13.07% for the employee's personal social security contribution.

steps.title: Taxable Base
steps.description: Calculating the taxable amount after social security and personal allowances.

steps.title: Withholding Tax (Précompte)
steps.description: Applying progressive tax brackets (25% to 50%) based on the 'Barème/Barema' charts.

steps.title: Net Benefits Addition
steps.description: Adding tax-free reimbursements, representation allowances, and deducting the personal share of meal vouchers.

items.text: Non-taxable Allowances: Costs 'proper to the employer' (e.g., home office, internet) can add €150+ to the net without increasing tax.
Family Situation: Having a non-working spouse or dependent children significantly reduces the monthly withholding tax.
The Bonus 'Net-Net': Under the CLA 90 scheme, companies can pay an annual performance bonus with very favorable tax treatment.
Intellectual Property (IP) Rights: Some professions can receive part of their compensation as IP rights, taxed at an effective rate of ~7.5% - 15% (subject to strict caps).

faqs.question: What is the 13.92 monthly system?
faqs.answer: It refers to 12 months of salary + 13th month (end-of-year bonus) + double holiday pay (~0.92 month).

faqs.question: How accurate are online net calculators?
faqs.answer: They provide good estimates, but the final payslip may vary based on exact tax-free representation allowances and commuting costs.

items.title: Marital Status
items.text: Marriage and dependent children significantly impact net salary.

items.title: Commuting
items.text: Bicycle and public transport allowances are often tax-free.

items.title: IP Rewards
items.text: Certain creative roles can receive tax-optimized IP payments.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Belgium
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Incorporation in Belgium
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Incorporation in Belgium.

steps.title: Drafting the Financial Plan
steps.description: Creating a detailed 2-year business prospect to prove the company's financial viability (mandatory for SRL/BV).

steps.title: Opening a Blocked Bank Account
steps.description: Depositing the initial capital in a 'blocked' Belgian account until incorporation is finalized.

steps.title: Notarial Deed Execution
steps.description: Signing the incorporation deed before a Belgian notary and registering it with the Registry of Legal Entities.

steps.title: CBE/KBO Registration
steps.description: Obtaining a unique enterprise number from the Crossroads Bank for Enterprises.

steps.title: VAT Activation
steps.description: Applying for a VAT number (TVA/BTW) through a business counter (Guichet d'entreprises/Ondernemingsloket).

steps.title: UBO Filing
steps.description: Registering the ultimate beneficial owners in the national UBO register within 30 days.

items.text: The SRL (Société à Responsabilité Limitée) / BV (Besloten Vennootschap) is the most common form, requiring no minimum statutory capital (but 'sufficient' initial equity).
Language of the Deed: The deed must be in the language of the region (Dutch for Flanders, French for Wallonia).
The SA (Société Anonyme) is preferred for larger ventures planning to go public, requiring at least €61,500 in capital.
Branch vs. Subsidiary: A branch (succursale) is faster to set up but the parent company remains 100% liable for Belgian debts.
Directors' Liability: Directors can be held personally liable for gross negligence or failure to pay social security contributions.

faqs.question: How long does it take to incorporate in Belgium?
faqs.answer: Usually 2-4 weeks, depending on the speed of opening the blocked bank account and notary availability.

faqs.question: What is a 'sufficient' capital for an SRL?
faqs.answer: It must be justified by the financial plan. If the company fails within 3 years due to insufficient capital, founders can be held liable.

faqs.question: Can I incorporate remotely?
faqs.answer: Yes, through a power of attorney, though the signatures must be legalized/apostilled if signed abroad.

items.title: Language
items.text: Articles of Association must be in the regional language.

items.title: Bank Account
items.text: Share capital must be deposited in a blocked account first.

items.title: VAT

items.text: War for Talent: High demand for STEM profiles and healthcare professionals leads to aggressive counter-offers.
Company Cars: Despite tax changes, the company car remains a highly sought-after status symbol and tax-efficient benefit.
Work-Life Balance: Belgians value the 'right to disconnect' and flexible remote work options (1-3 days per week is standard).
Job Hopping: While mobility is increasing, many Belgian professionals still value long-term stability with a single employer.
Multilingualism: In Brussels, fluency in at least two of the three main languages (FR/NL/EN) is often a non-negotiable requirement.

faqs.question: What is the typical notice period for candidates?
faqs.answer: Highly variable based on seniority and sector, but usually ranging from 6 weeks to 3+ months for senior roles.

faqs.question: Are trial periods allowed for new hires?
faqs.answer: Since 2014, formal trial periods have been abolished for most indefinite contracts, replaced by shorter notice periods in the first months.

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors instead of full-time employees?
faqs.answer: Yes, but be careful of 'false self-employment' (faux indépendance) which is strictly monitored by social security inspectors.

items.title: Job Ads
items.text: Often posted in Dutch, French, and English.

items.title: Sickness
items.text: Employer pays guaranteed salary for the first month of illness.

items.title: Notice
items.text: Notice periods are calculated in weeks based on seniority.

faqs.question: Does the HRIS handle Dimona declarations?
faqs.answer: Most modern HRIS platforms in Belgium automate this or sync with the social secretariat who handles it.

faqs.question: Are digital signatures legally binding?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Qualified Electronic Signatures' (QES) are fully recognized for all labor-related documents.

faqs.question: What is the standard accounting year in Belgium?
faqs.answer: Most companies follow the calendar year (Jan 1 - Dec 31), though any 12-month period is permitted.

faqs.question: Is an audit mandatory for all companies?
faqs.answer: No, only for 'large' companies meeting specific thresholds related to employee count, turnover, and assets.

faqs.question: Can I keep my books in English?
faqs.answer: While English is common in business, the official filing and chart of accounts must follow Belgian GAAP (PCMN) standards.

items.text: The ITAA (Institute for Tax Advisors and Accountants) is the regulatory body for chartered accountants in Belgium.
Electronic invoicing (Peppol) is becoming mandatory for B2B transactions in Belgium starting 2026.
Annual accounts must be drafted in the language of the company's registered office (Dutch, French, or German).

items.title: Filing
items.text: Annual accounts filed with the NBB are public data.

items.text: Workplace Rules (Arbeidsreglement/Règlement de travail): Every employer must have one, defining work hours, holidays, and disciplinary procedures.
Risk Assessment: Companies must perform a formal psychosocial and ergonomic risk assessment for all workstations.
Whistleblowing: Companies with 50+ employees must implement a secure internal reporting channel.
CPBW/CE: Committees for Prevention and Protection at Work are required for companies with 50+ employees.
The 'Wellbeing at Work' Act: Covers not only physical safety but also psychosocial risks like stress and burnout.
Social Inspections: Belgian labor inspectors have broad powers to enter premises and request all social documents without prior notice.
Whistleblower Protection: New 2023 regulations require companies with 50+ employees to have internal reporting channels.
E-signature validity: Employment contracts must be signed via a qualified electronic signature (e.g., itsme or electronic ID card).

items.title: Prevention Advisor
items.text: Every company must have a Prevention Advisor (internal or external).

items.title: Work Rules
items.text: The 'Arbeidsreglement' is a mandatory document for all staff.

items.title: Social Elections

steps.title: Advance Tax Payments

steps.title: Annual Client Listing

steps.description: Filing municipal or provincial taxes (e.g., office space tax) depending on location.

items.text: Participation Exemption: Belgium offers 100% exemption for dividends received from qualifying subsidiaries (DRD regime).
R&D Incentives: Partial exemption from withholding tax for researchers is one of Belgium's most attractive tax features.
Capital Gains: Capital gains on shares are generally 100% tax-exempt for companies if conditions are met.
Notional Interest Deduction: Though significantly reduced, it still allows for a deduction based on the increase in equity.
Anti-Avoidance: Belgium strictly applies the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD).

faqs.question: What is the 'super-deduction' for R&D?
faqs.answer: It allows companies to deduct a percentage of R&D investments or patents from their taxable income.

faqs.question: Do I need a local tax resident director?
faqs.answer: While not strictly mandatory for all entities, it significantly helps in establishing 'substance' to avoid tax residency disputes.

faqs.question: Are there tax incentives for expats?
faqs.answer: Yes, Belgium has a specific 'Expat Tax Regime' (RSII/RSIIE) for qualified inbound researchers and executives.

items.title: Advance Payments
items.text: Pay quarterly to avoid corporate tax surcharges.

items.title: R&D
items.text: Highly attractive tax credits for research and development.

steps.title: Jurisdiction Clause
steps.description: Defining Belgian courts (usually Brussels) as the sole jurisdiction for B2B dispute resolution.

steps.title: Intellectual Property Clause
steps.description: Ensuring automatic transfer of all moral and economic rights for work created by employees/contractors.

steps.title: Non-Compete/Non-Solicitation
steps.description: Drafting enforceable clauses that strictly adhere to Belgian validity conditions (geographic range, time limit, and compensation).

steps.title: Liability Limitation
steps.description: Capping damages to insurance limits or annual contract value to protect the enterprise.

steps.title: Service Level Agreements (SLA)
steps.description: Specifying uptime and support response times for IT and software delivery contracts.

items.text: Language Priority: In Flanders, contracts with employees must be in Dutch. In Wallonia, French. In Brussels, the employee's language choice (FR/NL) or both.
Liability Caps: Total liability for damages is often capped at the level of insurance coverage (BA Uitbating).
Non-Compete Enforceability: Must be limited in time (12 months max), space (national), and include a compensatory payment (min 50% salary).
The 'B2B Law' of 2019: Prohibits unfair contract terms between companies, similar to B2C consumer protection.
Language of the Contract: While B2B contracts can be in English, a Dutch or French version is often required for labor-related MSAs.
Copyright vs. Author's Rights: Belgium has strong protection for authors; explicit written transfer of rights is non-negotiable.
The 2023 Civil Code Reform: Important changes to contract law principles regarding 'hardship' (imprévision) clauses.

faqs.question: Which court has jurisdiction for master agreements?
faqs.answer: Typically the Commercial Court of the district where the defendant's registered office is located (e.g., Brussels, Antwerp).

faqs.question: Can electronic signatures be used?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Qualified Electronic Signatures' (QES) via itsme or eID are legally equivalent to handwritten ones under the eIDAS regulation.

items.text: The Language Divide: Marketing in Belgium is effectively marketing to two different countries with distinct media landscapes.
High Digital Maturity: Belgium has one of the highest e-commerce penetration rates in Europe.
Privacy First: Belgian consumers are highly sensitive to data privacy and GDPR compliance in marketing communications.
Brussels as a Hub: Campaigns centered on the capital should consider a more international, English-speaking audience.
Visual Aesthetics: Belgian design often balances minimalist Northern European styles with creative Southern influences.

faqs.question: Do I need separate agencies for Flanders and Wallonia?
faqs.answer: Many large agencies are bilingual, but some brands prefer specialized 'regional' partners for deep cultural resonance.

faqs.question: Is English-only marketing effective in Brussels?
faqs.answer: Effective for the expat bubble, but broad market penetration requires Dutch and French.
